Subject: Re: Evidence request — Evidence scope and KMS clarifications

Laura / Bridgewell team — looping in the security details you asked about. Short answers up front: 

- Subprocessors: we will provide a CSV with name, country, function, and whether the vendor has access to plaintext customer data.
- Dataflow: we will annotate the inference path. For hosted API customers, requests traverse our front-end, are routed to the inference runtime, and persistent storage for logs/metrics is in our telemetry stack; PII is redacted per customer config. For Dedicated/Private customers we can show region pinning and VPC peering paths.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (CMKs) in AWS KMS. For CMKs the customer retains control of the key policy and rotation; we only receive wrapped DEKs. We also have an HSM-backed option for Dedicated customers — notes attached.

Attachments we'll provide in this thread:
- bridgewell-subprocessor-roster-20261022.csv (includes access level flags)
- bridgewell-dataflow-diagram-annotated.vsdx (annotated with transit/at-rest boundaries)
- SOC2-TypeII-2025-redacted.pdf (redacted to remove internal test data and client names)
- sig-lite-responses-bridgewell.xlsx (SIG control mapping + answers)
- kms-pathing-and-hsm-notes.md (technical note on key flows and HSM eligibility)

Please note an item: if Bridgewell requires "onshore-only" subprocessors for certain functions (e.g., logging, data archival), we can mark those in the CSV but some telemetry/storage partners operate multi-region; we can propose an onshore-only scope or a dedicated instance.

Laura — confirm whether you want the SOC2 redaction to strip cryptographic material and any internal infra diagrams beyond our annotated dataflow. We can make a minimal redaction version if needed to speed delivery.

-Marissa
Director, InfoSec Controls
Redwood Inference
